video_title: Stewie & Myles on the NBA Finals, Liberty Win Streak & When to Get Mad!

quotes.speaker: Myles Turner
quotes.summary_phrase: Myles Turner on Jalen Brunson's mastery of angles and floor reading
quotes.excerpt: he's always been a master of angles. His center of gravity is real low.
quotes.quote: I've always been a fan of Jalen Brunson's game. He's always been a master of angles. His center of gravity is real low. He reads the floor really well. In today's day and age, a pure point guard is so hard to come across. There's only a few that are left in the league. Maybe three or four can play their pure point guards, but you're able to mix that with someone who's also a pure scoring threat. That's everything you want in a floor general.

quotes.speaker: Myles Turner
quotes.summary_phrase: Myles Turner on why Jalen Brunson is so successful with the Knicks
quotes.excerpt: he's going to make sure he gets 25 to 30 shots a game, and his team allows him
quotes.quote: I think that he's so successful because he gets to his spots. He's going to make sure he gets 25 to 30 shots a game, and his team allows him to be him. There's no one that's stepping on his toes. All the role players know exactly what they're supposed to do, and they know that he's the guy.

quotes.speaker: Myles Turner
quotes.summary_phrase: Myles Turner on Jaylen Brown's role in Knicks culture
quotes.excerpt: he embodied that New York culture just because of who he was and where he was from.
quotes.quote: Guys don't even talk about the Charles Oakleys of the world. He's not the greatest Knick ever, but he was part of the culture. You obviously have the Carmelo Anthonys of the world. He didn't get to the heights that Jalen Brunson did, but he embodied that New York culture just because of who he was and where he was from. You obviously got the Patrick Ewings, Willis Reed, Walt Frazier.

quotes.speaker: Myles Turner
quotes.summary_phrase: Myles Turner on the mental and physical toll of NBA playoff series
quotes.excerpt: mentally, emotionally, you're exhausted, bro. Side-to-side movement. People don't realize just like basketball is not just a one-dimensional sport.
quotes.quote: These guys are tired, bro. It's just what comes with it. Mentally, emotionally, you're exhausted, bro. Side-to-side movement. People don't realize just like basketball is not just a one-dimensional sport where you're sprinting up and down the floor. Sliding laterally and what not, you're playing on different linear planes. That takes a lot out of you, bro. Nothing can prepare you for this time of the year. Wembanyama is only 22 years old.

quotes.speaker: Breanna Stewart
quotes.summary_phrase: Breanna Stewart on how fatigue leads to late-game mistakes
quotes.excerpt: that fatigue is what leads to late-game mistakes. So that's what led to the bad turnover.
quotes.quote: That fatigue is what leads to late-game mistakes. So that's what led to the bad turnover, things like that, because you just get lost in it for a second.

quotes.speaker: Myles Turner
quotes.summary_phrase: Myles Turner on Karl-Anthony Towns' offensive growth
quotes.excerpt: the thing that KAT has done offensively that's opened up his game so much is passing.
quotes.quote: The thing that KAT has done offensively that's opened up his game so much is passing. He's passing the shit out the ball, bro. He's passing the ball so well. I think that he's always been someone who wanted to be the primary scorer. He's an outside threat, he wants to shoot his threes, his step-backs. He's really answered the call when it comes to his role. He's not trying to do too much.

quotes.speaker: Myles Turner
quotes.summary_phrase: Myles Turner on Jaden McDaniels' defensive impact
quotes.excerpt: Jaden McDaniels is in there, it's kind of throwing them off his balance, throwing off his feet.
quotes.quote: Jaden McDaniels is in there, it's kind of throwing them off his balance, throwing off his feet. Mitch is huge. He's a great defender. He's someone who can kind of knock you off, and he knows his role. He's in there to get in your head.

quotes.speaker: Myles Turner
quotes.summary_phrase: Myles Turner on Jaden McDaniels' defensive versatility
quotes.excerpt: he doesn't look like he has the frame to be as physical as he is, but he's a physical defender.
quotes.quote: You look at someone like Jaden McDaniels, he doesn't look like he has the frame to be as physical as he is, but he's a physical defender. He gets into you, he picks up. He's got really long arms and he's been an X-factor for them too, man. He's playing at a high level as well.

quotes.speaker: Myles Turner
quotes.summary_phrase: Myles Turner on Josh Hart's role as an X-factor
quotes.excerpt: he gets like the really big rebounds, he gets the really big stops.
quotes.quote: A living example of X-factor is obviously Josh Hart. I think that he's someone, I don't even think he scored last game, but he gets like the really big rebounds, he gets the really big stops. He goes down in transition and pushes. He knows his role to a T.

quotes.speaker: Myles Turner
quotes.summary_phrase: Myles Turner on Landry Shamet's impact
quotes.excerpt: Landry Shamet really came in and answered the call, man. He's hit some big shots.
quotes.quote: Landry Shamet really came in and answered the call, man. He's hit some big shots. He's a physical defender, and he's more than just a shooter.

quotes.speaker: Myles Turner
quotes.summary_phrase: Myles Turner on De'Aaron Fox's injury impact
quotes.excerpt: Fox hasn't been the same Fox because of his ankle. He's a very explosive athlete.
quotes.quote: Fox hasn't been the same Fox because of his ankle. He's a very explosive athlete. I think when Jalen Brunson and Fox start talking shit to each other, it kind of woke Fox up a little bit and he kind of started going at it himself.

quotes.speaker: Breanna Stewart
quotes.summary_phrase: Breanna Stewart on team adjustments in playoff games
quotes.excerpt: if you start the game soft and then try to get more physical or more aggressive, then you're going to get called for all those fouls later.
quotes.quote: If you start the game soft and then try to get more physical or more aggressive, then you're going to get called for all those fouls later.

quotes.speaker: Myles Turner
quotes.summary_phrase: Myles Turner on the importance of forgetting previous games
quotes.excerpt: you have to forget about the last two games, because we've had two days to pass.
quotes.quote: You have to forget about the last two games, because we've had two days to pass. That's the difference between the finals and all these other playoff series. In other playoff series, it's game off, game off, game off. Now it's game, you're off for two days, now you have to sit here and think about what you did for two days.

quotes.speaker: Myles Turner
quotes.summary_phrase: Myles Turner on the need for teams to attack the paint
quotes.excerpt: we have to touch the paint at least once a possession, no matter what.
quotes.quote: The biggest thing I would probably say is that we have to touch the paint at least once a possession, no matter what. Transition threes, cool, let that shit fly, this is what y'all do. But offensively, we have to try to find a way to break that plane, to break that free throw line.

quotes.speaker: Myles Turner
quotes.summary_phrase: Myles Turner on how attacking the paint creates perimeter opportunities
quotes.excerpt: if you do get into the paint, they overhelp and they're going to overcommit.
quotes.quote: If you do get into the paint, they overhelp and they're going to overcommit. And then that's when you start getting perimeter threes or what not, because they're okay giving up top of the break threes and everything. It's a low percentage shot. But that's when the better shots start to come in is when you do break that plane and kind of pass the ball out as opposed to moving the ball around the horn and never touching the paint.

quotes.speaker: Breanna Stewart
quotes.summary_phrase: Breanna Stewart on defensive adjustments and ball screens
quotes.excerpt: I had A'ja on me last night, and you know, as a center, a five, she doesn't want to be guarding ball screens.
quotes.quote: I had A'ja on me last night, and you know, as a center, a five, she doesn't want to be guarding ball screens. Trying to contort their defense in a different way than they've ever practiced. And if it helps like calm and comfort the team, I can definitely get us initiated and set up into things, especially when it's just Pauline and I basically at the point for now.

quotes.speaker: Myles Turner
quotes.summary_phrase: Myles Turner on the evolution of centers initiating offense
quotes.excerpt: it's something that's so much more common now than when it used to be when you first got to the league.
quotes.quote: It's something that's so much more common now than when it used to be when you first got to the league. Bigs handling the ball, bigs initiating offense. You see a lot of that in EuroBall, so this is nothing new. I know it's something that you've been capable of doing for a long time, but to be able to do it when your team is relying on you the most, that's a different level of composure that you've got to get to as a player.

quotes.speaker: Myles Turner
quotes.summary_phrase: Myles Turner on the importance of adjusting to refereeing
quotes.excerpt: you kind of adjust to the way the game is being called, and that's just a part of being a pro.
quotes.quote: You kind of adjust to the way the game is being called, and that's just a part of being a pro. So it's nothing new.

quotes.speaker: Breanna Stewart
quotes.summary_phrase: Breanna Stewart on the importance of consistency in playoff basketball
quotes.excerpt: right now, it's just about like consistency, you know, from night in to night out.
quotes.quote: Right now, it's just about like consistency, you know, from night in to night out, knowing that it's like, all right, are we going to be like physical or are we going to have to like change the way that we're trying to blow up some things, blow up some DHOs.

quotes.speaker: Myles Turner
quotes.summary_phrase: Myles Turner on the importance of getting to the free throw line
quotes.excerpt: all the best players in our league and your league, they know how to get to the line.
quotes.quote: All the best players in our league and your league, they know how to get to the line. If you miss three or four shots in a row, you just got to see the ball go in. The easiest way to do that is getting to the line. And I don't think that's something that should necessarily be too criticized in a sense. It's just a way of playing the game and a way of getting smart, especially in those crunch-time moments.
